prolonged intake of ethanol is accompanied by essentially no alterations of total amounts of brain or liver ribosomes or of brain tRNA.

prolonged ingestion of ethanol by rats results in a change in the quantitative distribution of the isoacceptor species of leucine tRNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of prolonged ingestion of ethanol on the ribosomal and tRNA components of rat brain.
the effects of prolonged ingestion of ethanol on the brain and liver ribosomal systems of rats.
the question of the possible involvement of the tRNA system in ethanol-induced changes in brain protein metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results of the experiments reported here indicate a change in isoacceptor distribution of leucine tRNA in brain, but no changes in the total tRNA, the ribosomal RNA, or the activities of several amino acyl-tRNA synthetase activities.
ethanol intake does not alter the overall protein synthetic capacity of the brain but may affect some specific steps in the translation process.
prolonged ingestion of ethanol in rats is not associated with major changes in brain ribosomes and transfer RNA, but that a change in the distribution of isoacceptor tRNA species may occur.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the brain of the rat is capable of adapting to prolonged ethanol ingestion with no apparent changes in the total amounts of ribosomes or tRNAs, but with some changes in the quantitative distribution of the isoacceptors of leucine-tRNA.
the effects of ethanol on brain protein biosynthesis are not mediated via ribosomes or tRNA.
prolonged ingestion of ethanol does not cause major alterations of ribosomes and tRNAs in rat brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain tRNA is not the only thing that can be altered by prolonged ethanol intake.
prolonged intake of small quantities of ethanol does not affect the total amount of tRNA or the total amount of ribosomal RNA, but does alter the isoaccepting tRNAs.
the isoaccepting leu tRNA species change with chronic alcohol exposure, but this change is specific to brain tissue.
